paper_title: Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for the Neural Architecture Search model proposed by the paper?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports 62.4 test perplexity for the best Neural Architecture Search model on Penn Treebank; Table 2 also reports 64.0 and 67.9 for other Neural Architecture Search configurations.
sub_questions.quote: Our cell achieves a test set perplexity of 62.4 on the Penn Treebank, which is 3.6 perplexity better than the previous state-of-the-art model.

sub_questions.q: In what evaluation setting does the paper report Penn Treebank test perplexity for the Neural Architecture Search model, such as single model, ensemble, dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, or fine-tuning?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports the Neural Architecture Search results in Table 2 as single model perplexity; the paper does not report dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning for the Neural Architecture Search model on Penn Treebank.
sub_questions.quote: Table 2: Single model perplexity on the test set of the Penn Treebank language modeling task.

sub_questions.q: Which Neural Architecture Search configuration achieves the 62.4 Penn Treebank test perplexity, and what configuration details are reported?
sub_questions.answer: The 62.4 result is Neural Architecture Search with base 8 and shared embeddings, 54M parameters; the paper also reports Neural Architecture Search with base 8 at 67.9 with 32M parameters and Neural Architecture Search with base 8 and shared embeddings at 64.0 with 25M parameters.
sub_questions.quote: Neural Architecture Search with base 8 and shared embeddings 54M 62.4

sub_questions.q: Which baseline in the paper's Penn Treebank comparison table has the lowest listed test perplexity?
sub_questions.answer: The best listed baseline is Zilly et al. 2016 - Variational RHN, shared embeddings, with 66.0 test perplexity.
sub_questions.quote: Zilly et al. 2016 - Variational RHN, shared embeddings 24M 66.0

sub_questions.q: How does the best Neural Architecture Search Penn Treebank test perplexity compare with the best baseline listed in the paper?
sub_questions.answer: The best Neural Architecture Search result, 62.4 test perplexity, is 3.6 perplexity better than the previous state-of-the-art baseline, Zilly et al. 2016 Variational RHN with shared embeddings at 66.0; the paper states that the models found by Neural Architecture Search outperform other state-of-the-art models on this dataset.
sub_questions.quote: the models found by Neural Architecture Search outperform other state-of-the-art models on this dataset, and one of our best models achieves a gain of almost 3.6 perplexity.

sub_questions.q: Does the paper report dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning for the Neural Architecture Search model on Penn Treebank?
sub_questions.answer: No. The paper reports single-model perplexity for Neural Architecture Search; dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, and fine-tuning are not reported for the Neural Architecture Search model on Penn Treebank. Cache/pointer appears only among baseline labels such as Pointer Sentinel-LSTM.
